raw.assessment: The incumbent combines staffed key collection with telephone or in-person booking and recurring room allocations. Eleven groups obtaining weekly bookings supports partial effectiveness (H4-O1); inherited times may aid predictability, but that benefit is unmeasured. H4-O2 limits an account based solely on exhausted aggregate capacity: calendars showed 68% reserved and 14 sessions were late or unattended. This does not establish usable spare capacity, because peak demand, acceptable alternatives and equipment requirements remain unknown (H4-O3, H4-O5). Recorded conflicts and administration averaging 127.5 minutes weekly exceed the stated targets; the 90% needs measure cannot be calculated from bookings alone.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a single authoritative desk ledger with numbered reservation/change confirmations and a clearly dated online copy could reduce conflicting expectations while retaining telephone and in-person access.
openings.delta: Make each change traceable to one confirmed room, date, time and contact, including confirmation that a released reservation is cancelled.
openings.prediction: Conflicts attributable to stale or inconsistent reservation records should decline; conflicts persisting despite matching confirmations would weaken this explanation.
openings.probe: Use supplied notes and short contact conversations to reconstruct the three conflicts. Then record confirmation agreement for each new conflict and total weekly administration, testing whether the procedure fits the two-hour limit.
assumptions: The desk can maintain one authoritative ledger using existing resources.
Confirmation handling costs less time than it saves; this requires measurement.

openings.claim: Do declined groups have acceptable, equipment-compatible windows that overlap currently unused time, or is their demand confined to already occupied periods?
openings.delta: Distinguish calendar vacancies from rehearsal time that actually meets expressed needs, including the group missing suitable slots.
openings.prediction: Compatible vacancies would support reassignment as a useful mechanism; exclusively occupied acceptable windows would instead demonstrate a timing or equipment bottleneck.
openings.probe: Ask each contact for weekly rehearsal needs, all acceptable windows and necessary equipment. Map these onto the existing calendar, preserving performances and every requesting group's 60-minute entitlement; calculate the maximum attainable needs coverage before proposing changes.
assumptions: Contacts can state needs accurately enough for an eight-week feasibility check.
Unattended bookings are not treated as released, and outside rehearsals are not assumed to satisfy needs.

raw.assessment: Unused aggregate capacity does not establish usable capacity. Missing time windows, equipment requirements, and attendance dependencies prevent distinguishing allocation problems from genuine scarcity. Neither opening yet demonstrates the eight-week targets.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: reserve a suitable rehearsal capability at a fixed time, with the room assigned before arrival, so piano-independent groups can voluntarily exchange rooms without moving their rehearsal times.
openings.delta: Separate the time commitment from room identity; blank equipment fields must be resolved rather than treated as no requirement.
openings.prediction: Some declined piano-dependent requests become feasible through same-time room reassignment, with no loss of another group's acceptable rehearsal time.
openings.probe: Ask contacts for necessary equipment and acceptable windows. Replay the nine refusals against both rooms, allowing only consented room exchanges. Count newly feasible requests and minutes spent. Pilot only confirmed exchanges, issuing matching paper and online records plus telephone or in-person confirmation; preserve each requested weekly 60-minute entitlement and both performances.
assumptions: Both groups' confirmed equipment requirements remain satisfied.
Confirmation can fit the two-hour weekly administration target.

openings.claim: Some apparently independent group reservations may compete for the same essential musicians, making overlapping bookings unusable even when rooms are available.
openings.delta: Treat shared-person availability as a possible scheduling constraint alongside rooms and group contacts.
openings.prediction: Late or missed sessions disproportionately coincide with another commitment involving an essential shared member; absent this pattern, the hypothesis weakens.
openings.probe: During short contact conversations, ask whether each late or missed session involved such a clash and which time windows avoid recurrence; compare with attended sessions. Test whether a paper schedule avoiding confirmed clashes still meets stated needs and every requested weekly entitlement within existing hours, equipment, and protected performances. Record interview and rescheduling time.
assumptions: Groups may share essential members; this is unobserved.
Reported correlations would support further testing, not establish causation.

openings.claim: One authoritative desk ledger, numbered confirmations and a dated online copy may reduce conflicting expectations.
openings.discriminator: Record disagreements decline; conflicts with matching confirmations weaken the explanation.
openings.probe: Reconstruct three conflicts; track confirmed bookings, changes and cancellations, subsequent conflicts and weekly administration.
openings.uncertainty: Desk maintenance feasibility and net time savings are unknown.

openings.claim: Compatible vacancies versus occupied acceptable windows distinguish reassignment opportunities from timing or equipment scarcity.
openings.discriminator: Needs and equipment mapping reveals whether unused hours are usable.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints through bounded feasibility mapping.
openings.probe: Ask every contact for weekly needs, all acceptable windows and equipment; calculate maximum attainable coverage within protected commitments.
openings.uncertainty: Needs accuracy unknown; absence does not release bookings, and outside rehearsals do not establish satisfied needs.

openings.claim: Fixed-time capability reservations with consented room exchanges may accommodate piano-dependent requests.
openings.discriminator: Refusals become feasible without losing another group's acceptable time or required equipment.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints if exchanges are confirmed before arrival.
openings.probe: Resolve blank equipment fields; replay nine refusals across both rooms; count feasible exchanges and effort. Pilot confirmed exchanges with matching calendars and telephone or in-person confirmation.
openings.uncertainty: Room preferences may be nonnegotiable; administrative fit remains unproven.

openings.claim: Shared essential musicians may make simultaneous group reservations unusable.
openings.discriminator: Late or missed sessions coincide disproportionately with shared-member commitments compared with attended sessions.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints in a paper scheduling test.
openings.probe: Ask session-specific causes and clash-free windows; test a schedule avoiding confirmed clashes; record interview and rescheduling time.
openings.uncertainty: Member overlap is unobserved; recall and correlation cannot establish causation.

post_distill.decision: Measure feasibility first. All tests retain two rooms, 24 staffed hours, requested weekly 60-minute access, telephone/in-person changes, existing equipment, no new fees and both performances. No opening demonstrates eight-week targets: needs coverage is unknown; three conflicts and 127.5 weekly administration minutes exceed targets.
